mode_meaning.contaminated: Team inputs are season-to-date leaderboards, so every graded game sits inside its own features. This measures calibration, not skill, and it cannot validate anything.
mode_meaning.vintage: Every game is priced on a leaderboard snapshot whose knowledge cutoff is strictly before that game: team offense, team run prevention, the listed probable and the park index all come out of that snapshot. A game with no such snapshot is skipped, not graded on today's numbers, and a game whose snapshot predates the stored park column is priced with the park term at neutral rather than on the live index. This is the only mode that can validate the model.

park_basis.note: the park index is read from each game's own vintage record; a record written before the park column existed prices its games on a NEUTRAL park (the park term drops out) rather than on the live index, which is the in-progress season and would leak the eval window into its own features

gates.why: the contaminated forward margin over the home-field baseline is +0.005794 Brier with a paired sd of 0.08647, so a margin that size needs 603 games to clear one-sided 95%; 600 is that number, and a clean margin will be smaller, so this is a floor and not a pass

gate.policy: min_edge stays null until all three gates are open. A threshold invented to make a pick appear is the single most dishonest number this module could publish.

validation.note: Two modes, both labelled. The in-sample and forward numbers are CONTAMINATED: their features are season-to-date leaderboards that contain the games being graded. The vintage number is the honest one and it graded 456 games. A pick threshold is set from the vintage mode or from nothing.
